name: app-store-scraper (facundoolano)
what_it_holds: Node.js library (MIT, 1422 stars, updated 12 Sep 2026) that hits Apple's public iTunes/App Store lookup and search endpoints with no auth/API key. Returns per-app fields including current category rank, rating count (proxy for cumulative review count), rating average, price, and version history for any app id -- e.g. Airbnb's iOS app id 401626263, plus Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia. No data committed; a scheduled run would need to be built to accumulate a rank/review-count time series.
why_useful: Same rationale as the Google Play scraper above but for iOS -- lets us build an Airbnb iOS app review-count/rating time series as an engagement proxy (gap #5) without touching airbnb.com.
themes: Airbnb reviews text corpora and review-date datasets on GitHub (review counts over time as a stays proxy)

Fills gap #5 (engagement: app downloads/rankings) and gap #14 (app-store review scrapers) as a zero-cost, no-login method to build our own point-in-time panel of Airbnb's and competitors' App Store rank and review-count going forward from whenever we start running it; does not backfill history.

Addresses gap 5 (engagement: app rankings/reviews) and gap 14 (app-store review scrapers) as a acquisition method for point-in-time snapshots of ABNB's App Store standing; would need to be run repeatedly by us to build a time series, and per repo rules that scraping decision is left to a human.

Could be run periodically going forward to build an Airbnb-app category-ranking / rating-count time series as a downloads/engagement proxy (gap 5); does not backfill history (no historical dataset committed), only forward point-in-time snapshots.

Directly answers the 'app release-notes scraper' theme: `versionHistory` gives Airbnb's iOS release cadence and changelog text, which can be timestamped to flag feature launches (e.g. new product lines, RNPL rollout, regional expansion mentions) ahead of earnings commentary -- a genuinely point-in-time-able series since Apple's version-history is itself dated.

CONTEXT gap #5 wants app download/ranking history as an engagement proxy for Airbnb's own app; this tool can pull Airbnb's current App Store rank/rating/review volume on a schedule to build a point-in-time series going forward (does not recover history retroactively), and the review text stream is a free sentiment/complaint source (e.g. cancellation/RNPL friction mentions).

Same engagement-proxy use case as gplay-scraper but for iOS App Store rankings/reviews -- category-level 'Travel' chart position is a genuinely non-Airbnb-branded engagement series that could be tracked for Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking, Expedia together.

name: google-play-scraper

No auth needed, no data committed.
why_useful: Same as the iOS counterpart -- free, no-key method to build a going-forward Android download/rank/review-count time series for Airbnb vs. Booking/Expedia/Vrbo; the most-starred, most actively maintained project in this space, with a whole family of derivative wrappers (see google-play-api, JoMingyu port).

name: appstorecat
what_it_holds: Self-hosted, open-source (MIT) 'app intelligence toolkit' with a Docker/MySQL/Redis stack. Explicitly does per-app 'App rankings' with 'per-app pivot across countries x collections x categories' and 'daily snapshots of top free/paid/grossing' for both App Store and Google Play, plus keyword density and locale-change tracking. 227 commits, 39 stars. No data committed to the repo itself — you self-host and it accumulates history in your own DB going forward.
why_useful: Closest thing found to a genuine rank-HISTORY tool: if stood up now it would start building a daily top-charts + per-app rank time series for Airbnb's travel-category rank on both stores, directly targeting gap 5's 'app downloads/rankings history'. It only starts collecting once deployed — no backfill of past ranks.

name: crux-dumps
what_it_holds: Monthly Chrome UX Report (CrUX) popularity-rank dumps as .txt.xz files, one per rank threshold (top 1k/5k/10k/...), covering Feb 2021 - Aug 2026 monthly. Each row is origin + numeric popularity rank (real Chrome-browser usage based, not a modeled estimate). Recent monthly files ~17-19M entries, 85-97 MiB compressed. Free mirror of data that otherwise needs a BigQuery export.
why_useful: Gives a monthly, real-user popularity-rank time series for airbnb.com (and vrbo.com, booking.com, expedia.com, vacasa.com etc.) back to 2021 with no API key or BigQuery bill — directly fills gap #5 (web-traffic/engagement proxy) and is genuinely point-in-time (dated monthly snapshots, not a pulled-today number), unlike Google Trends which the team already found unusable because it isn't point-in-time.
